display_name: Galidor - Defenders of the Outer Dimension (USA) (En,Fr,De,Es,It,Nl,Sv,Da)

slots_and_copies.name: header
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Always present. Logical byte 0 is magic 0x28; bytes 1-2 are the big-endian checksum. Validated first by FUN_08023a24 at 0x08023a24 via FUN_0802368c read at EEPROM offset 0.

slots_and_copies.name: sector_0_global
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Always read at boot by FUN_08007f20 (0x08007f20) via FUN_080239c0 sector 0. If its u32 word 0 != 0x28 the game initialises it and writes sectors 0-4. Its word 5 selects which profile sector (1-4) is loaded next.

slots_and_copies.name: sector_1_profile
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded by FUN_08007f20 when sector_0 word 5 == 0 (sector index = word5 + 1). Written at first-boot format by FUN_08007f20 via FUN_08023928 sector 1 after FUN_08007e48 template init.

slots_and_copies.name: sector_2_profile
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded when sector_0 word 5 == 1. Written at first-boot format by FUN_08007f20 via FUN_08023928 sector 2; word 21 incremented to 1 before this write.

slots_and_copies.name: sector_3_profile
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded when sector_0 word 5 == 2. Written at first-boot format by FUN_08007f20 via FUN_08023928 sector 3; word 21 incremented to 2 before this write.

slots_and_copies.name: sector_4_profile
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded when sector_0 word 5 == 3 (guard in FUN_08007f20 is word5 < 4). Written at first-boot format by FUN_08007f20 via FUN_08023928 sector 4; word 21 incremented to 3 before this write.

slots_and_copies.name: trailing_unused
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Never addressed by sector reads/writes (sectors end at 503). Zero in both samples; covered by the whole-image checksum. Written only by FUN_080237e0 format, which zeroes 64 blocks x 8 bytes = 512 bytes.

checksums.name: eeprom_sum16_be
checksums.formula_detail: In logical EEPROM space (see report: logical byte i = raw .sav byte (i//8)*8 + (7 - i%8), i.e. each 8-byte block reversed): stored = (logical[1]<<8)|logical[2] (big-endian u16). Computed = (sum of logical bytes 3..511 inclusive) & 0xFFFF. Implemented by FUN_08023830 at 0x08023830: first reads EEPROM offset 3 length 8 and sums its first 5 bytes (offsets 3-7), then loops reading 8 bytes at offsets 8,16,24,... summing all 8, while offset <= bound in _DAT_080238a8. FUN_08023928 at 0x08023928 writes it back at EEPROM offset 1 as bytes [sum>>8, sum&0xFF] via FUN_08023720(1, buf, 2). FUN_08023a24 compares CONCAT11(byte1,byte2) against FUN_08023830() & mask and reformats via FUN_080237e0 on mismatch. NOTE: algorithm enum has no sum16_be option; sum16_le is the closest enum value and endianness is fully specified here - storage is big-endian, summation is byte-wise so operand endianness does not apply.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 transfer: param1=src, param2=dst, param3 = halfword count | 0x80000000 (enable). Saves/restores a control register, programs DMA src/dst/count via _DAT_080279e0/_DAT_080279e4/_DAT_080279e8 (DMA3 registers, cf. 0x040000D4 block), busy-waits on bit 0x8000 of the count/control halfword. Used both to clock bitstreams into EEPROM at 0x0D000000 and to read them back.

EEPROM read one 8-byte block: block address param1 (masked 16-bit, must be < block count at struct+4). Builds serial bitstream (two 1 start bits + address bits, count = byte at struct+8) in a stack array of u16 0/1 entries, DMA-writes it to 0x0D000000 via FUN_08027970(buf, 0x0D000000, addr_bits+3), then DMA-reads 0x44 halfwords back via FUN_08027970(0x0D000000, buf, 0x44) and unpacks 64 serial bits into 4 u16 values stored descending from param2+6. This descending-u16 unpack is why each raw .sav 8-byte block is the reverse of logical EEPROM byte order. Returns 0 on success.

EEPROM write one 8-byte block: expands 4 u16 data words (64 bits) plus block address bits into a serial bitstream (leading 1 start bit, 0 bit, address bits descending, then data bits), DMA-writes addr_bits+0x43 halfwords to 0x0D000000 via FUN_08027970, calls FUN_080278a4, then polls the EEPROM data line (uRam0d000000 & 1) / a status byte for write completion (returns an error sentinel on timeout), then calls FUN_0802792c. Returns 0 on success.
EEPROM verify: re-reads block via FUN_080279f0 into a stack buffer and compares all 4 u16 words against the caller buffer; returns 0 if identical, 0x8000 on mismatch.

Auxiliary DMA/interrupt channel setup around the EEPROM write busy-wait (manipulates channel pointer registers and a bit 8<<channel in a control register). No save data passes through it. Static-only identification.
Auxiliary DMA/interrupt channel teardown matching FUN_080278a4 (clears the 8<<channel bit, restores saved control value). No save data. Static-only identification.
Plain byte memcpy (src, dst, len) used to extract/insert sub-ranges of 8-byte EEPROM blocks. Note argument order is flipped between its two callers.

EEPROM ReadBytes(byte_offset, dst_ram, len): validates dst!=0, len>=1, offset <= limit; converts offset to block = offset>>3 and intra-block = offset&7; per 8-byte chunk reads the block with FUN_080279f0 and verifies with FUN_08027b7c (up to 3 attempts each, i.e. retry counter reaching 2 fails), then FUN_0802366c copies the requested slice to RAM. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

EEPROM WriteBytes(byte_offset, src_ram, len): read-modify-write per 8-byte block - reads block (FUN_080279f0 + FUN_08027b7c verify, 3 attempts), FUN_0802366c inserts the new bytes, writes with FUN_08027aa0 (3 attempts), verifies again with FUN_08027b7c (3 attempts). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
Checksum computer: sums logical EEPROM bytes 3..end (see checksums entry) via repeated FUN_0802368c reads; returns -1 if any read fails, otherwise the 32-bit running sum (callers mask it to 16 bits).

Sector writer WriteSector(ram_buffer, sector_index): if sector_index == 0x400 sentinel, uses last-written sector + 1 (tracked in _DAT_080239a8). Computes EEPROM offset = sector_size * sector_index + 3, writes the sector with FUN_08023720 (length argument = sector size, dropped by the decompiler in this call), recomputes the checksum with FUN_08023830 and stores it big-endian at EEPROM offset 1 via FUN_08023720(1, buf, 2), then records the sector as last-written. Guarded by a busy flag at _DAT_080239a0. Returns 1 or -1 (0xFFFFFFFF). Ghidra displays some calls with the trailing argument missing - see report.

Sector reader ReadSector(ram_buffer, sector_index): if sector_index == 0x400 sentinel, uses last-read sector + 1 (tracked in _DAT_08023a0c). Reads sector_size bytes from EEPROM offset sector_size * sector_index + 3 via FUN_0802368c (length argument dropped by decompiler) and records the sector as last-read. Returns 1 or -1. Guarded by a busy flag at _DAT_08023a08.

EEPROM/sector-system init and whole-image validation InitSectors(sector_size): requires 1 <= sector_size <= 511, stores it, calls FUN_08027804(4) and FUN_0802786c(2, ...) config helpers, reads header block at EEPROM offset 0 via FUN_0802368c. If byte 0 == 0x28 ('('), recomputes FUN_08023830 and compares (byte1<<8)|byte2; on mismatch (or any failure) formats via FUN_080237e0 and marks the state dirty (*_DAT_08023a88 = 1). If byte 0 != 0x28, formats via FUN_080237e0 unconditionally. Returns a division result via FUN_0802dfe4 (software divide, not save logic). Called by the game as FUN_08023a24(100), fixing sector size = 100 bytes.

Format/erase: writes an 8-byte block with byte 0 = 0x28 and bytes 1-7 = 0 at EEPROM offset 0 via FUN_08023720(0, buf, 8), then writes zeroed 8-byte blocks at offsets 8,16,...,504 (loop counter 1..0x3F shifted left 3) - i.e. zeroes the full 512-byte EEPROM, leaving only the magic byte. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

SDK config helper called with argument 4 during FUN_08023a24 init; writes one of three register/pointer values depending on whether the argument is 4, 0x40, or other (returns 1 in the other case, which aborts init). Exact register identity unresolved in the decompilation. Static-only.

SDK config helper called with argument 2 during FUN_08023a24 init; for argument <= 3 stores the argument, computes a table pointer arg*4 + base, and returns a config word through the out-pointer; returns true (non-zero) for argument > 3, which aborts init. Exact semantics unresolved. Static-only.

Game profile-template initialiser FUN_08007e48(slot_arg): zeroes u32 words 0..20 of the profile RAM buffer (pointer from _DAT_08007e88), sets word 21 = slot_arg, sets word 0 |= 0x10000000 (so profile byte +3 becomes 0x10), words 22-23 = 0, word 24 = a value read from another struct (+0xC), and mirrors that value into a table at slot_arg*4 + base + 0x28. Called once with argument 0 by FUN_08007f20 before the sector 1-4 format writes.

Game save-system boot/load (no callers in the traced 140-function corpus; reached from game code outside the corpus or via pointer). Calls FUN_08023a24(100), reads sector 0 into the global RAM buffer, validates its word 0 == 0x28, loads the selected profile sector, or else initialises sector 0 defaults and writes sectors 0-4. See caller_chains.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot/load, validation path: FUN_08007f20 calls FUN_08023a24(100) (sector size 100). FUN_08023a24 reads the 8-byte header at EEPROM offset 0 and, if byte 0 == 0x28, verifies the checksum. Mapping method: the calls appear in ghidra/decompiled.c as func_0x08023a24 / func_0x0802368c aliases; ghidra/callgraph.json does not record them (it keys the same bodies as FUN_08023a24 etc. with empty caller lists), so callers were mapped by text-searching decompiled.c for the func_0x aliases and matching addresses.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Text search of ghidra/decompiled.c for 'func_0x08023a24', 'func_0x0802368c', 'FUN_080279f0' etc., cross-checked against ghidra/callgraph.json callees of 0x0802368c (0x0802366c recorded; the EEPROM calls appear only as func_ aliases in the C text).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot/load, checksum verification inside FUN_08023a24: FUN_08023830 sums logical bytes 3..511; result masked and compared against (byte1<<8)|byte2 read from offset 0. On mismatch FUN_080237e0 reformats the whole EEPROM (this is the mechanism behind the PACKET cold-reload probe: raw .sav offset 0x5 is logical byte 2, the checksum low byte, so mutating it forces a reformat to blank, exactly as observed: reverted_to_blank_on_mutation=true, save_rewritten_after_mutation=true).
caller_chains.how_mapped: Read of FUN_08023a24 and FUN_08023830 bodies in ghidra/decompiled.c (lines 3768-3815 and 3649-3685); covered range and byte order corroborated by exact Python checksum matches on both .sav files.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot/load, happy path: after init, FUN_08007f20 reads sector 0 (EEPROM offset 3, 100 bytes) into the global RAM buffer via FUN_080239c0(buffer, 0). If buffer word 0 == 0x28 and word 5 < 4, it reads profile sector word5+1 (sectors 1-4) into a second RAM buffer (uRam08007fe4 in the decompilation). No RAM fields are mutated on this path - EEPROM bytes are deserialised verbatim (FUN_0802366c byte copy) into the two 100-byte RAM structs.
ram_fields_updated: profile_ram_buffer[0..24] (filled by read of sector word5+1, not mutated)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Read of FUN_08007f20 body (ghidra/decompiled.c lines 2281-2337): func_0x080239c0(_DAT_08007fc8, 0), test *piVar1 == 0x28, test piVar1[5] < 4, then func_0x080239c0(uRam08007fe4, piVar1[5] + 1).

caller_chains.trigger_context: First boot / invalid sector 0: FUN_08007f20 takes the else branch, initialises the sector-0 RAM struct in place, then flushes it with FUN_08023928 (sector 0; the decompiler drops the trailing sector argument in this one call - the sector-0 destination follows from the offset formula and from the observed .sav layout). Each FUN_08023928 write also recomputes and rewrites the whole-image checksum at EEPROM offset 1 (chain continues 0x08023928 -> 0x08023830 and 0x08023928 -> 0x08023720 offset 1).
ram_fields_updated: sector_0 words 6,7,8,9 = 0 (loop from buffer+9 u32 downwards, 4 words)
sector_0 words 10,11,12,13 = -1 / 0xFFFFFFFF (loop from buffer+0xD u32 downwards, 4 words; +0xD is a byte offset in the decompiled pointer arithmetic on an int*, i.e. word 13)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Read of the else branch of FUN_08007f20 (lines 2299-2322). Word indices are piVar1[n] on an int* (byte offset = 3 + 4*n in EEPROM sector-0 space). The initialised values match the observed .sav sector 0 exactly for every word except words 10, 16 and 18, which gameplay had already mutated in both captures (see fields and report section 5) - words 10/16 start at -1 per this init and word 18 is not written here, so it starts at the formatted 0.

caller_chains.trigger_context: First boot / invalid sector 0, continued: FUN_08007e48(0) builds a blank profile template in the profile RAM buffer, then FUN_08007f20 writes it to sector 1, increments the u32 at buffer+0x54 (word 21) and writes sector 2, increments again and writes sector 3, increments again and writes sector 4. This exactly produces the observed profile sectors: word 0 = 0x10000000, word 21 = 0,1,2,3 for sectors 1,2,3,4, word 24 = 1, all other words 0 - identical in both .sav captures, proving no gameplay write to sectors 1-4 happened between the captures. FUN_08027aa0 internally calls FUN_080278a4 before polling the EEPROM and FUN_0802792c afterwards.
ram_fields_updated: profile word 21 = 0 (FUN_08007e48 arg), then incremented in RAM by FUN_08007f20 before each subsequent sector write: 1 for sector 2, 2 for sector 3, 3 for sector 4
profile word 24 = value copied from another RAM struct +0xC (FUN_08007e48; observed 1 in all four profile sectors in both saves)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Read of FUN_08007e48 (lines 2247-2274) and the tail of FUN_08007f20 (lines 2323-2331). buffer+0x54 byte offset = word 21. Observed .sav profile sectors match the predicted template byte-for-byte in both captures.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Every sector write: after the sector bytes are flushed via FUN_08023720, FUN_08023928 recomputes the whole-image checksum with FUN_08023830 and writes 2 big-endian bytes at EEPROM offset 1 via FUN_08023720(1, buf, 2). There is no per-sector checksum - integrity is global over bytes 3..511, so any sector mutation changes the header checksum (observed: the sector-0-only diff between the two captures moves the checksum from 0x1462 to 0x0C6C, a delta explained exactly by the byte diff, verified in Python).
caller_chains.how_mapped: Read of FUN_08023928 (lines 3692-3730): uStack_10 = sum>>8, uStack_f = sum&0xFF, FUN_08023720(1, &uStack_10, 2).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Invalid/missing/corrupt save at boot: FUN_080237e0 writes the 0x28 magic byte at EEPROM offset 0 and zeroes all remaining 504 bytes (64 blocks total), after which FUN_08007f20's else branch writes fresh sectors 0-4. This is the 'reverted to blank' behaviour confirmed by the PACKET mutation probe.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Read of FUN_080237e0 (lines 3607-3642) and its two call sites in FUN_08023a24 (lines 3794, 3798).

fields.name: header_magic
fields.update_mechanism: Written once by format (FUN_080237e0 writes block byte0=0x28, rest 0). Checked by FUN_08023a24: if != 0x28 the whole EEPROM is reformatted. Raw .sav offset 7 (block-reversed).
fields.evidence: FUN_080237e0 auStack_10[0]=0x28 (decompiled.c:3622); FUN_08023a24 cStack_18 == '(' i.e. 0x28 (line 3790). Both .sav files: logical byte 0 = 0x28 after reversing each 8-byte raw block.

fields.name: header_checksum_be
fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed and rewritten after every sector write by FUN_08023928 (FUN_08023830 sum, stored big-endian: byte1=sum>>8, byte2=sum&0xFF). Verified by FUN_08023a24 at boot; mismatch reformats the EEPROM. Raw .sav offsets 6 (high) and 5 (low).
fields.evidence: FUN_08023928 lines 3713-3715; FUN_08023a24 lines 3791-3794 CONCAT11(uStack_17,uStack_16). Python: sum(logical[3:512])&0xFFFF equals stored on both files (0x1462, 0x0C6C). PACKET probe at raw offset 0x5 = logical byte 2 (checksum low) reverted to blank, corroborating.

fields.name: sector0_word0_magic
fields.update_mechanism: Set to 0x28 in RAM by FUN_08007f20 else branch (*piVar1 = 0x28) then flushed via FUN_08023928 sector 0. On load, FUN_08007f20 tests *piVar1 == 0x28 to decide the save is initialised. Raw .sav offsets 4-7 block-reversed (low byte 0x28 at raw offset 4).
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 lines 2294, 2300. Both saves: logical bytes 3-6 = 28 00 00 00.

fields.name: sector0_word1
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to 1 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[1]=1) at first boot, flushed with sector 0. Semantics unknown - no other writer/reader in the traced corpus.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2301; observed 01 00 00 00 at logical 7 in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word2
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to 1 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[2]=1). Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2302; observed 1 in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word3
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to 1 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[3]=1). Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2303; observed 1 in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word4
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to 0 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[4]=0). Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2304; observed 0 in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word5_active_profile_index
fields.update_mechanism: Not written by the first-boot init (stays at the formatted 0). Read by FUN_08007f20: if < 4, profile sector word5+1 is loaded into the second RAM buffer. So word5 is the active profile selector (0-based). Any writer that changes it is outside the traced corpus.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 lines 2295-2296: (uint)piVar1[5] < 4 then FUN_080239c0(second_buffer, piVar1[5]+1). Observed 0 in both saves, consistent with sector 1 being the loaded profile.

fields.name: sector0_words6_9_zeroed
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed by FUN_08007f20 init loop (buffer+9 u32 downwards, 4 words = words 6-9). No observed mutation. Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 lines 2306-2311; zero in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word10
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to -1 by FUN_08007f20 (words 10-13 = -1 loop from buffer+0xD). Between the two captures it changed from -1 to 1 while words 11-13 stayed -1, so a gameplay writer outside the traced corpus mutated this word in RAM and sector 0 was re-flushed via FUN_08023928 (checksum updated accordingly). This is one of only three gameplay-mutated words observed. Semantics unknown - hypothesis: a progress/flag word whose low byte transitions -1 -> 1.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 lines 2312-2318 init; logical diff between captures at bytes 43-46 (0xFF.. -> 01 00 00 00 at word10, with word10 byte0 also changing) - precisely: logical offsets 0x2B-0x2E changed FF FF FF FF -> 01 00 00 00 for bytes 0x2B..0x2E is offset 43..46.

fields.name: sector0_words11_13_minus1
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to -1 each by FUN_08007f20 (same loop as word 10). Unchanged between captures. Semantics unknown; the -1 pattern suggests unused/empty slots (e.g. empty inventory or unassigned entries).
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 lines 2312-2318; FF FF FF FF x3 at logical 47-58 in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word14
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to 1 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[0xE]=1). Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2319; observed 1 in both saves.

fields.name: sector0_word15
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to 0 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[0xF]=0). Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2320; observed 0.

fields.name: sector0_word16
fields.update_mechanism: Initialised to -1 by FUN_08007f20 (piVar1[0x10]=-1). Changed -1 -> 0 between captures: gameplay mutation outside the traced corpus plus a sector-0 re-flush. Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007f20 line 2321; logical diff at offsets 67-70 (FF FF FF FF -> 00 00 00 00).

fields.name: sector0_word17
fields.update_mechanism: Not written by any traced function; 0 from format in both captures. Part of the 100-byte sector struct copied verbatim by FUN_080239c0/FUN_08023928.
fields.evidence: Zero in both saves; no writer in decompiled.c references sector word 17.

fields.name: sector0_word18
fields.update_mechanism: Changed 0 -> 1 between captures with no writer in the traced corpus: gameplay code outside the 140 functions mutated the RAM struct and re-flushed sector 0. Semantics unknown - hypothesis: a counter/flag incremented by early gameplay (only the low byte is ever non-zero in the samples).
fields.evidence: Logical diff at offset 75 (00 -> 01); both saves otherwise identical in sector 0 except words 10, 16, 18 and the checksum.

fields.name: sector0_words19_24_reserved
fields.update_mechanism: Zero from format; never mutated in the samples. Copied verbatim by sector read/write. Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: Logical bytes 79-102 all zero in both saves.

fields.name: profile_word0_flags
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_08007e48 zeroes profile words 0-20 then sets word0 |= 0x10000000 (byte +3 = 0x10 in EEPROM order). Same value at sector offsets 103, 203, 303, 403 (each +3 byte = 0x10). Hypothesis: bit 28 is a valid/initialised flag for a profile slot; only static evidence, no reader tests it in the traced corpus.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007e48 lines 2263-2264; logical bytes at 106, 206, 306, 406 = 0x10, all other word-0 bytes 0, in both saves and all four profile sectors.

fields.name: profile_words1_20_zero
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed by FUN_08007e48 template init; no gameplay mutation observed in either capture (profiles are still blank templates). This 80-byte span per profile sector (x4 sectors) is where per-profile progress would live, but every byte is unproven.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007e48 lines 2259-2262 zero words 0-20 (word 0 then ORed); logical profile bytes all zero in both saves.

fields.name: profile_word21_sector_counter
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_08007e48(0) sets word 21 = 0; FUN_08007f20 writes sector 1, then does *(int*)(buffer+0x54) += 1 (0x54 = 84 = word 21) before writing sectors 2, 3, 4 in turn. So at format time word 21 equals sector_index - 1. Whether gameplay reuses it as a real counter is unproven - it may simply be a stored copy of the slot number.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007e48 line 2263 (puVar1[0x15]=param_1); FUN_08007f20 lines 2325-2331 increments at iVar4+0x54 between sector writes. Observed 0,1,2,3 across sectors 1-4 in both saves - an exact match to the code, and the strongest proof of the 100-byte sector geometry.

fields.name: profile_words22_23_zero
fields.update_mechanism: Set to 0 by FUN_08007e48 (words 22, 23). Semantics unknown.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007e48 lines 2265-2266; zero in both saves.

fields.name: profile_word24
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_08007e48 copies a u32 from another RAM struct (+0xC) into profile word 24 and mirrors it into a table entry for the slot. Observed value 1 in all profiles. Semantics unknown (hypothesis: a version, count of something, or a pointer-derived small integer - the source struct is unresolved).
fields.evidence: FUN_08007e48 lines 2267-2269; logical bytes 199, 299, 399, 499 = 01 00 00 00 in both saves.

fields.name: trailing_bytes_503_511
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed by format only; read only as part of the checksum sum. Because they are zero, the exact checksum loop end (last block read at offset 504 vs 496) cannot be distinguished from the samples - see open questions.
fields.evidence: Sectors end at 3 + 5*100 = 503; bytes 503-511 zero in both saves; FUN_080237e0 zeroes 64 blocks.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: In logical space set byte 0 to 0x29 (raw .sav: offset 7, currently 0x28, set to 0x29). Do NOT repair the checksum - byte 0 is outside the covered range 3..511, so the checksum stays valid and only the magic test can catch it.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_08023a24 sees byte0 != 0x28 and calls FUN_080237e0: full reformat. Predicted observable: game boots to a blank/first-boot state, .sav rewritten to the formatted image (logical byte0=0x28, rest 0, then fresh sectors 0-4 written by FUN_08007f20), sector-0 word5 profile selection lost. This isolates the magic check from the checksum check.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit in the stored checksum, e.g. logical byte 2 ^= 0x01 (raw .sav offset 5 - exactly the PACKET probe offset).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Already confirmed by the PACKET cold-reload probe (integrity_check_confirmed, reverted_to_blank_on_mutation, save_rewritten_after_mutation): FUN_08023a24 checksum mismatch -> FUN_080237e0 reformat -> FUN_08007f20 writes fresh sectors 0-4. Game presents as a new/blank save.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set sector-0 word 18 (logical offset 75, u32 LE) from its cap-01 value 1 to e.g. 2, then repair the checksum: recompute sum(logical[3:512])&0xFFFF and store big-endian at logical 1-2 (raw offsets 6,5). Raw-file procedure: reverse each 8-byte block, edit, recompute, reverse back.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Boot passes validation (FUN_08023a24) and sector 0 loads. Observable depends on the unknown semantics of word 18: watch for a changed counter/flag in UI or RAM (the 100-byte sector-0 RAM buffer pointed to by _DAT_08007fc8). If nothing changes, word 18 is likely a passive progress marker. A crash or reformat would mean the word is range-checked outside the traced corpus.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set sector-0 word 10 (logical offset 43) back to 0xFFFFFFFF in the cap-01 save (undoing the observed -1 -> 1 transition), with checksum repair as above.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests whether word 10 gates anything: if the gameplay event that set it to 1 re-triggers or a UI element reverts, word 10 is a one-shot progress flag. Also try setting words 11-13 (offsets 47,51,55) from -1 to 0/1 one at a time with repair - if they are empty-slot sentinels, the game may treat the slot as occupied (possible phantom entry or crash, which itself is diagnostic).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set sector-0 word 5 (logical offset 23) to 1, 2, 3 in turn, with checksum repair. Also try 4 (out of range).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: For 1-3: FUN_08007f20 should load profile sectors 2, 3, 4 respectively instead of sector 1 - observable as a different profile buffer in RAM (all templates are near-identical, so distinguish by first writing a marker, e.g. profile word 21, into the target sector with repair). For 4: the word5 < 4 guard fails, so no profile is loaded - predicted the game proceeds with whatever the second RAM buffer held (zeroed/stale), a testable difference.
